cards.explanation: The answer is servants. Paul and Timothy, the two who send this letter, open with "…servants of Christ Jesus…" (Philippians 1:1) No big title up front, just servants. I stand on a gold base in a tall chef's hat and I'd still rather be known as the guy who stamps cookies.

The answer is that he thanks his God, every single time. Paul says, "I thank my God every time I remember you." (Philippians 1:3) Think about that for a second, friends. Every time they come to his mind, he thanks God. I wish my memory did that when I think about my first batches of cookies.

The answer is False. Paul writes, "In every prayer for all of you, I always pray with joy…" (Philippians 1:4) All of them are in his prayers, not just a few, and he prays with joy. That's one big prayer list, and I'd need a bigger cookie box just to hold the names.

The answer is partners. Paul thanks God "…because of your partnership in the gospel from the first day until now…" (Philippians 1:5) Partners means they're in it together with him. A partner shows up with the dough, not just the opinions.

The answer is that God will carry it on to completion. Paul is confident that "…He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus." (Philippians 1:6) Notice who is doing the carrying, friends. God started it, and He finishes it. That's a lot more comforting than a batch I started and forgot about in the oven.

The answer is that he has them in his heart. Paul says it's right to feel this way "…since I have you in my heart." (Philippians 1:7) That's his reason. It comes from how close he holds them, and it reads like a hug in letter form.

The answer is True. Paul writes, "God is my witness how I long for all of you with the affection of Christ Jesus." (Philippians 1:8) He doesn't just say he misses them. He names God as his witness. That's a serious way to say "I mean it."

The answer is knowledge and depth of insight. Paul prays "that your love may abound more and more in knowledge and depth of insight…" (Philippians 1:9) He wants love that keeps growing and knows what it's doing, friends. I'd call that a love with its apron on and its recipe in hand.

The answer is best. Paul prays that they "…may be able to test and prove what is best and may be pure and blameless for the day of Christ…" (Philippians 1:10) That means telling what's truly best, not just what's close. I wish I had that skill when I'm staring at a tray of cookies that all look done.

The answer is Jesus Christ. Paul wants them "…filled with the fruit of righteousness that comes through Jesus Christ…" (Philippians 1:11) The fruit comes through Him. That takes the pressure off, because nobody has to squeeze it out alone.

The answer is God. Paul closes by saying the fruit is "…to the glory and praise of God." (Philippians 1:11) The whole prayer ends pointing straight at Him, friends. That's the last word of the prayer, and it belongs to God.
